column2: It is a sideline to the cheese shop, but for the horn you can count on me.
The friend who played Mozart's horn concertos. Mozart scribbled jokes in the score such as 'Leutgeb the ass'.
Mozart: Oboe Quartet
The oboe is the instrument closest to the human voice.
The Mannheim oboe, for your orchestra.
An oboe virtuoso of the Mannheim school. Mozart wrote his Oboe Quartet for him.
Harp
Harp concerto
I am also at work on improving the harp.
The strains of the harp, for your orchestra.
A harp virtuoso from Bohemia. In Paris he also worked on improving the instrument and greatly widened the harp's music.
Mozart: piano concerto
I cannot see, but I see every note.
Let me play in your orchestra.
A Viennese pianist and singer who lost her sight in early childhood. A friend of Mozart and Salieri, she later devoted herself to musical education for the blind.
Caprices for cello
Since I fitted an endpin to the cello, everything has been easier.
The Paganini of the cello, for your orchestra.
A Belgian virtuoso called 'the Paganini of the cello'. He is credited with popularising the endpin that rests the cello on the floor.
Cello études
Études? I have plenty more to write.
The bass of Dresden, for your orchestra.
Principal cellist of the Dresden court. His études are still a road every cello student must travel.
Berlioz: Harold en Italie
I play the organ in church as well.
The melancholy of the viola, for your orchestra.

A violist and organist of Paris. He gave the first performance of the solo part in Berlioz's Harold en Italie. A devout man, he is said to have played at the Opéra with his back turned so as not to see the stage.
Piano Concerto No. 1
I offered to give young Chopin three thorough years of lessons, you know.
The foremost piano in Paris, for your orchestra.
The grand old man of the piano in Paris and a partner in the firm of Pleyel. He urged Chopin to study with him for three years and was refused.
Piano solos
My engagement to Monsieur Berlioz is ancient history.
In your orchestra I shall play brilliantly.
A celebrated woman pianist of Paris. She was engaged to Berlioz but married the piano maker Pleyel, to Berlioz's fury.
Piano concerto
Chopin and Liszt are both my friends.
My Paris connections and all, for your orchestra.
A German pianist active in Paris. A friend in common of Chopin, Liszt and Mendelssohn.
Even a harp can sound like an orchestra.
A revolution on the harp, for your orchestra.
An English virtuoso called 'the Liszt of the harp'. Berlioz praised him to the skies.
Guitar
Variations on a Theme from Die Zauberflöte
The guitar is a small orchestra.
The Spanish guitar, for your orchestra.
The great master of the Spanish guitar. Active in Paris and London, he was called 'the Beethoven of the guitar'.
The Boehm system? The old flute is quite enough for me.
The flute of Paris, for your orchestra.
The leading flautist of the Paris Opéra and Conservatoire. He opposed the new Boehm flute to the last.
Elfentanz
My wife is Liszt's favourite pupil, Sophie Menter.
The brilliance of the cello, for your orchestra.
A celebrated cellist from Prague. Principal at the Vienna Court Opera, later professor at the Budapest Academy.
12 Caprices
I am a regular at London's Monday Popular Concerts.
The foremost cello in London, for your orchestra.
A great cellist, born in Italy and based in London. In 1844 Liszt, impressed that he was playing on a borrowed instrument, gave him an Amati cello.
Brahms: Cello Sonata No. 2
I am the cellist of the Joachim Quartet.
The bass of Berlin, for your orchestra.
Cellist of the Joachim Quartet. He later gave the premiere of Brahms's Double Concerto with Joachim.
Tchaikovsky: Variations on a Rococo Theme
I have touched up young Tchaikovsky's score a little.
The cello of the Moscow Conservatory, for your orchestra.
Professor of cello at the Moscow Conservatory. He gave the premiere of Tchaikovsky's Rococo Variations, but angered the composer by reordering them on his own authority.
Liszt: Piano Concerto No. 1
Maestro Liszt told me I was his finest pupil.
Art schooled by Liszt, in your orchestra.
The favourite pupil Liszt called his 'only daughter', one of the finest women pianists of her day. Her husband was the cellist Popper.
Piano pieces
I train my pupils hard.
A great teacher's ear, for your orchestra.
A great teacher who had studied with Czerny. In Vienna he later trained Paderewski and Schnabel.
Grieg: Piano Concerto
At the age of eight I played before President Lincoln.
The passion of Venezuela, for your orchestra.
A woman pianist from Venezuela. As a girl she played for Lincoln at the White House. She was called 'the Valkyrie of the piano'.
The horn in Wagner's Tristan und Isolde
I dislike Wagner's music. Though I play it well enough.
The finest horn in Germany, for your orchestra.
Principal horn of the Munich court orchestra and father of R. Strauss. Famous for detesting Wagner, though the composer himself acknowledged his playing.
Hohe Schule des Violoncellospiels
I teach young people in Budapest.
A great professor's cello, for your orchestra.
A celebrated professor at the Budapest Academy. His études are still required study for cellists.
Hymnus for cello ensemble
I have played at the Gewandhaus for more than 30 years.
The tradition of Leipzig, for your orchestra.
Principal cellist of the Gewandhaus Orchestra and a great teacher. He later trained Feuermann and Piatigorsky.
Haydn: cello concerto
With Señor Casals… a good deal has happened.
The passion of Portugal, for your orchestra.
A Portuguese woman cellist. Known as Casals's companion, she later became enormously popular in Britain.
Viola solos (arrangements)
I will not have the viola called the instrument of failed violinists.
The solo viola, in your orchestra.
The pioneer who raised the viola to a solo instrument. Many composers wrote viola works for him.
Ballet: Pohádka (Fairy Tale)
I play the viola in the Czech Quartet.
The inner voices of Bohemia, for your orchestra.
Violist of the Czech Quartet and a pupil of Dvořák. He was later active as a composer and conductor.
I have married four times, but to the piano I have been faithful.
The Valkyrie of the piano, for your orchestra.
A great pianist called 'the Valkyrie of the piano'. She lived in Berlin and trained many pupils, MacDowell among them.
I am of Maestro Liszt's last generation of pupils.
Art straight from Liszt, for your orchestra.
A pupil of Liszt's last years. A great pianist who went on playing at the highest level for a long time.
53 Studies on Chopin's Études
I shall play you a Chopin étude with the left hand alone.
The pianist's pianist, for your orchestra.
A transcendent technician called 'the pianist's pianist'. He arranged Chopin's études to make them harder still.
Chopin: Piano Concerto No. 1
I am as good at sarcasm as I am at the piano.
Transcendent technique, for your orchestra.
A transcendent technician of Liszt's school. Equally famous for his sharp tongue.
My wife Rosina is a pianist too.
The piano of Moscow, for your orchestra.
Winner of the 1895 Rubinstein Competition. He later taught at the Juilliard School with his wife Rosina.
Ravel: Jeux d'eau
Ravel and I have been friends since we were children.
Let us premiere new music with your orchestra.
A pianist from Spain. He gave the first performances of one work after another by Ravel and Debussy.
Schubert: piano sonatas
I want to play music that is better than it can be played.
Deep music, in your orchestra.
A pupil of Leschetizky. He later made the first recording of all Beethoven's piano sonatas.
If there is no music for the harp, I write it myself.
The sound of the harp, for your orchestra.
A French harp virtuoso. Her own harp concerto greatly widened the possibilities of the instrument.
Debussy: Prélude à l'après-midi d'un faune
I have only just arrived in New York.
The French flute, for the New World and for your orchestra.
A French flute virtuoso. He played in the premiere of Debussy's Prélude à l'après-midi d'un faune and crossed to New York in 1905.
Bach's organ works
I have just finished my book on Bach. Now I shall study medicine.
Bach's organ, for your orchestra.
Organist and theologian. In 1905 he published his study of Bach and the same year began studying medicine to become a doctor. He later devoted himself to medical work in Africa.
The great cellist Alborea, known as Francischello, has died.
The horn virtuoso Punto has died in Prague.
Mozart: Sinfonia concertante (violin and viola), K. 364
Solo viola
Haydn: Cello Concerto No. 2 in D major
Mozart: Horn Concerto No. 4
Solo horn
Mozart: Clarinet Concerto, K. 622 (1791)
Berlioz: Harold en Italie (solo viola)
Dvořák: Cello Concerto
Horn and woodwind
principal cellist of Haydn's orchestra
written for Kraft, principal of the Esterházy orchestra
the viola virtuoso Stamitz excelled in sinfonie concertanti for exactly these forces
written by Mozart for his friend Leutgeb
the last concerto, written for Stadler
written for Baermann and premiered by Baermann
Urhan gave the first performance of the solo; the work began as a commission from Paganini
premiered by Fitzenhagen (who reordered it on his own authority)
a masterpiece handed on by one great cellist after another
Nicolò Amati, 1649
Stradivarius 'Messiah', 1716
Guarneri del Gesù 'Il Cannone', 1743
Stradivarius cello 'Davidov', 1712
Jacob Stainer, 1668
The Tyrolean master. In the 18th century his instruments fetched more than Stradivari's, and Bach, too, is said to have owned a Stainer.
A new violin by Stradivari
In his Cremona workshop the aged Stradivari is still finishing new instruments. In those days it was simply 'an instrument by a living master'.
Stradivarius 'Lipiński', 1715
A great instrument said to have been played by Tartini and to have passed through his pupils into Lipiński's hands.
Stradivarius 'Viotti', 1709
The violin beloved of Viotti, father of modern violin playing.
Stradivarius 'Dolphin', 1714
Named for varnish that shimmers like a dolphin. Heifetz later played it.
Stradivarius 'Joachim', 1714
A violin played by Joachim.
Stradivarius 'Sarasate', 1724
Left by Sarasate in his will to the Paris Conservatoire. It is still in the instrument museum in Paris.
Stradivarius 'Gibson', 1713
Huberman's instrument. It was later stolen twice and was missing for half a century.
Stradivarius 'Kreutzer', 1731
A late Stradivari said to have been played by R. Kreutzer.
Stradivarius 'Lady Blunt', 1721
Scarcely played, it remains as it was when made.
Guarneri del Gesù 'Vieuxtemps', 1741
Beloved of Vieuxtemps; among the supreme masterpieces of del Gesù.
Guarneri del Gesù 'Ysaÿe', 1740
Ysaÿe's instrument. Later played by Isaac Stern.
Guarneri del Gesù 'de Bériot', 1744
An instrument from del Gesù's very last years.
Guarneri del Gesù 'Kreisler', 1733
Played by Kreisler, who later gave it to the Library of Congress.
